result.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
result.summary: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PRIME 框架：在检查前预先固定「证据路线」，用独立程序记录每次检查结果并拒绝结果无法支撑的结论，同时指引或代执行可支撑更强结论的检查；在 480 个公开记录任务上，受规则授权约束的结论均获支持，且指引与追加检查把合理结论得分从 30.1 提升至满分 59.2。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉或多模态状态，但其「预承诺证据路线＋外部账本拒绝未证实结论＋主动补查至停止」的机制，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、latent 假设取舍与停止决策提供可核查的推理期控制线索。
